near_miss.lead: Ir. tascrad feda 'overthrowing of trees' ~ ON felldu ... viðu 'felled trees'
near_miss.why_not: Different verbs (do-scara vs fella), fid ~ viðr cognate but 'fell trees' is everyday language; contexts unrelated (nature-description verse vs. saga battle).

near_miss.lead: ON vitni bera ~ AV punar ā bhara (prāṇam)
near_miss.why_not: Only *bʰer- shared; 'bear witness' vs 'bring back breath' are unrelated collocations.

near_miss.lead: lists of kin (father, mother, brother, sister, daughter); ON law 'drepr föður eða móður ... systur' ~ AV mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā (kin-slaying)
near_miss.why_not: Inherited kin terms naturally co-occur in any enumeration of family; no shared figure beyond the list. The kin-slayer category (ON law vs AV) uses non-cognate verbs (drepa vs han-) and is a universal legal/moral topic.

near_miss.lead: ON verja oddi ok eggju 'defend with point and edge'
near_miss.why_not: The Irish partner is a homiletic passage on sins with no relation. Ir. rind ⁊ faebur 'point and edge' is the semantic match but neither word is cognate with oddr/egg; a natural weapon merism.

near_miss.lead: Ir. beirid mac (do X) 'bore a son (to X)' ~ ON '... ól su kona barn'
near_miss.why_not: The ON verb is ala (context before: 'ól su kona barn'), not bera; barn < *bʰer- is only a derivative. 'Bear a child' with *bʰer- is lexical usage shared by Celtic and Germanic, not phraseology.

near_miss.lead: *h₁nómn̥ + *bʰer-: Ir. bertha ainm do 'a name was given to him' ~ ON nafn bera 'bear a name/title'
near_miss.why_not: Irish beirid/do-beir ainm (do) means 'bestow a name', an Irish-internal sense of 'carry to/give'; the ON (and Ved./Gk, see search lead) sense is 'bear, hold a name'. Different collocation, and the Irish pivots of BS-5e7e5/BS-63714 (sén maith; fled; m-bertha 'would be brought') share nothing with it.

near_miss.lead: cutting ribs: ON skerr ... rifjum ~ Serb. rebra presjekao
near_miss.why_not: Non-cognate verbs (*sker- vs *sek-), and the ON is eating a rib of meat, the Serbian a wound in battle; generic.

near_miss.lead: ON með orðum eða verkum 'by words or deeds' (merism; verk ~ Gk ἔργον)
near_miss.why_not: No partner in slab (AV Indra-strength litany is unrelated); 'word and deed' in ON law is also likely shaped by Latin verbo et opere, so not claimable as inherited.

near_miss.lead: Ir. cath (cuirid cath, cath coscrach) ~ OE heaþu (Beo. 1863 hringnaca ofer heaðu bringan)
near_miss.why_not: Only *kéh₃tu- shared; OE ofer heaðu in Beo. 1863 is usually emended to heafu 'seas', and heaþu- 'battle' is otherwise compound-only; Irish 'cuirid cath' 'joins battle' has no OE counterpart in the line. No shared phrase.

near_miss.lead: Ir. sén maith 'good omen' / fled ... m-bertha ~ ON orð ... bera
near_miss.why_not: No shared collocation; only *bʰer- and 'good' roots recur.

error.correct_reading: iomchur, verbal noun of imm-beir 'carry' (brú iomchuir 'womb of carrying'), < imm + *bʰer-
error.evidence: Old Irish imm-beir / immchor 'carrying'; 'brú iomchuir' = pregnant womb.

error.correct_reading: ra-airg, pret. 3sg of orgaid 'plundered, destroyed' (object Dún Sobairchi)
error.evidence: Parallel to ro marb in the same sentence; cf. 'oirg' lemmatized orcaid in mga:celtic-journal-revue-celtique-1870-1928:revueceltique22pari:L3105-L3107.
Lemma string carries the name marker twice.

search_lead.cognate: ON bera nafn = Ved. nā́ma bhar- (bibharti) = Gk ὄνομα φέρειν, all *bʰer- + *h₁nómn̥ in the sense 'bear (hold) a name/title'
search_lead.argument: ON uses bera + nafn productively in native prose for holding a rank or name (konungs nafn, tígnar nafn, bónda nafn, þræls nafn); RV has 8 cases of nā́ma bhar-, often with an evaluative adjective (śrútyam 'famous', gúhyam 'secret'), Greek tragedy has ὄνομα (δυσκλεές) φέρειν. Exact cognates in the same verb+object relation and sense across three branches; but 'bear a name' is an easy metaphor (cf. Lat. nomen ferre/gerere), so weak evidence of inheritance.
